---
title: "Task types"
description: "The task types an Automation can run — agents, SQL and semantic queries, conditionals, HTTP requests, pipelines, and sub-automations"
---

Every task declares a `type` that selects the tool it runs. This page covers the
core task types; iteration lives on the [Loops](/guide/build/automations/loops)
page.

## `type: agent`

Runs an [agent](/guide/build/agents) with a prompt.

| Component          | Description                                                                                                                                                                       | Type                       |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| agent_ref          | Path to the `.agentic.yml` agent to run, relative to the project root.                                                                                                            | required for `type: agent` |
| prompt             | The input prompt passed to the agent for this task.                                                                                                                               | required for `type: agent` |
| consistency_run    | Number of times to run the agent and select the most consistent output. Must be > 1 to enable.                                                                                    | optional (default: 1)      |
| consistency_prompt | Custom evaluation prompt for consistency checking. Overrides Automation-level prompt. Supports Jinja templating with variables: `submission_1`, `submission_2`, `task_description`. | optional                   |
| output.mode        | `answer` (default) returns the agent's natural-language answer. `sql` stops once the agent has produced SQL and returns the SQL text instead. See [SQL output mode](#sql-output-mode). | optional (default: `answer`) |

### Agent task consistency runs

You can enable consistency checking on agent tasks by setting `consistency_run`
to a value greater than 1. This runs the agent multiple times with the same
prompt and selects the most consistent output:

```yaml
# Automation-level consistency prompt (applies to all agent tasks)
consistency_prompt: |
  Your custom evaluation prompt here...
  Use {{ submission_1 }}, {{ submission_2 }}, and {{ task_description }}

tasks:
  - name: calculate_revenue
    type: agent
    agent_ref: analytics.agentic.yml
    prompt: "What was our total revenue last quarter?"
    consistency_run: 5 # Run 5 times and pick the most consistent result

  - name: analyze_trends
    type: agent
    agent_ref: analytics.agentic.yml
    prompt: "What are the key sales trends?"
    consistency_run: 3
    # Task-level prompt overrides Automation-level prompt
    consistency_prompt: |
      Compare these trend analyses focusing on directional consistency:
      Submission 1: {{ submission_1 }}
      Submission 2: {{ submission_2 }}
      Are they factually consistent? Answer A or B.
```

This is particularly useful for:

- Critical calculations where consistency is important
- Data analysis tasks that may have slight variations in output
- Queries involving complex logic where you want to verify the agent's reasoning

**Consistency prompt configuration:**

- **Automation-level**: Add `consistency_prompt` at the root to apply to all agent tasks
- **Task-level**: Add `consistency_prompt` to a specific task to override the Automation prompt
- **Default**: If not specified, uses the built-in evaluation prompt optimized for data analysis (view the [default prompt source](https://github.com/oxy-hq/oxygen-internal/blob/main/crates/core/src/config/constants.rs))

**Available template variables:**

- `{{ submission_1 }}` - First output
- `{{ submission_2 }}` - Second output
- `{{ task_description }}` - The task prompt

**Note:** Custom prompts completely replace the default. To adapt the default for your domain, copy the [source](https://github.com/oxy-hq/oxygen-internal/blob/main/crates/core/src/config/constants.rs) and modify the specific rules you need.

### SQL output mode

Set `output.mode: sql` to use an agent as a SQL generator. The agent stops once
it has SQL — skipping the natural-language answer — and the SQL text becomes the
task's result. SQL compiled from the semantic model or matched from a verified
query is returned without running it; SQL the agent wrote itself gets a
`LIMIT 0` check first. Pair it with [`cache`](#caching-a-tasks-output) to save
the SQL to a file and an `execute_sql` task to run it:

```yaml
tasks:
  - name: query
    type: agent
    agent_ref: analytics.agentic.yml
    prompt: Aggregate total weekly sales by month.
    output:
      mode: sql
    cache:
      enabled: true
      path: results/cache/monthly_sales.sql

  - name: run_query
    type: execute_sql
    database: local
    sql_file: results/cache/monthly_sales.sql
```

Automations that the agent would otherwise delegate to can't be used in SQL
mode.

## `type: execute_sql`

Executes a SQL query either referenced by filename or provided inline.

| Component | Description                                             | Type                          |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| sql_file  | The sql file within the `data` directory to execute     | required (or use `sql_query`) |
| sql_query | Inline SQL query to execute (alternative to `sql_file`) | required (or use `sql_file`)  |
| database  | The name of the `database` to execute the query against | required                      |

You can use either `sql_file` to reference a SQL file, or `sql_query` to provide
the SQL inline.
**Note:** These options are mutually exclusive—only one should be used at a time.
Specifying both in a single task is not allowed.

```yaml
# Using sql_file
- name: query_with_file
  type: execute_sql
  sql_file: my_query.sql
  database: local

# Using sql_query inline
- name: query_inline
  type: execute_sql
  sql_query: |
    SELECT * FROM users
    WHERE created_at > '2024-01-01'
  database: local
```

## `type: formatter`

Formats the provided `template` using the outputs of other `tasks`, then passes
the rendered template as output.

| Component | Description                                       | Type     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| template  | The template to be rendered and passed as output. | required |

## `type: workflow`

Runs another Automation as a sub-step.

| Component | Description                                                                          | Type     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| src       | Path to the Automation yml file to execute. Relative to the root of the oxy directory. | required |
| variables | Variables that are passed through, overriding the sub-Automation's variables.          | optional |

Use this to break up complex Automations into smaller, easily testable chunks.
The `variables` key allows parameterization by overriding the sub-Automation's
Automation-level variables. This is particularly useful when embedding an
Automation task into a loop:

```yaml
- name: loop_brands
  type: loop_sequential
  values: ["brand1", "brand2"]
  concurrency: 10
  tasks:
    - name: brand_stats
      type: workflow
      src: brand_stats.automation.yml
      variables:
        brand_rollup: "{{ loop_brands.value }}"
```

## `type: semantic_query`

Runs a query against your [semantic model](/guide/build/semantic-model/simple-model)
— measures, dimensions, filters, and ordering by name, with the SQL compiled for
you. See [Using the Semantic Model](/guide/build/semantic-model/use-in-agents#in-automations)
for every property.

```yaml
- name: sales_metrics
  type: semantic_query
  topic: sales
  dimensions:
    - orders.order_status
  measures:
    - orders.total_revenue
  limit: 10
```

Looker and Omni integrations add `looker_query` and `omni_query` task types —
see [Looker](/guide/build/connect-data/looker#using-looker-in-automations).

## `type: conditional`

Runs a different set of tasks depending on earlier results. Each branch's `if`
is a Jinja expression (without the surrounding braces) evaluated against the
outputs of previous tasks; the first truthy branch runs. An expression that
renders empty, `false`, `0`, or `none` is falsy.

| Component  | Description                                                        | Type     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| conditions | List of branches, each with an `if` expression and its own `tasks` | required |
| else       | Tasks to run when no branch matches                                | optional |

```yaml
- name: check_orders
  type: execute_sql
  database: local
  sql_query: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE created_at > current_date - 1

- name: alert_if_quiet
  type: conditional
  conditions:
    - if: check_orders.n[0] == 0
      tasks:
        - name: explain
          type: agent
          agent_ref: analytics.agentic.yml
          prompt: No orders came in yesterday. Check for upstream data issues.
  else:
    - name: summary
      type: formatter
      template: "{{ check_orders.n[0] }} orders yesterday."
```

## `type: http_request`

Makes an outbound HTTP request — for example, to post results to another
system's API. `url`, `headers`, `body`, and `form` values are Jinja templates
rendered against earlier task outputs, and `{{ secrets.NAME }}` resolves any
project [secret](/guide/manage/secrets) listed in `secrets`.

| Component         | Description                                                                                      | Type                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ |
| url               | Request URL                                                                                      | required                 |
| method            | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE`                                                       | optional (default: `POST`) |
| headers           | Request headers                                                                                  | optional                 |
| body              | Raw request body. Mutually exclusive with `form`                                                 | optional                 |
| form              | Form fields, sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`                                         | optional                 |
| secrets           | Names of project secrets to make available as `{{ secrets.NAME }}`                               | optional                 |
| timeout_secs      | Request timeout, 1–120 seconds                                                                   | optional (default: 30)   |
| expected_status   | Accepted status codes. When empty, any 2xx succeeds and anything else fails the task              | optional                 |
| allow_hosts       | Hostnames the request may target. When empty, any public host is allowed                          | optional                 |
| persist_to_secret | Write a field of the JSON response back to a project secret: `from` (a JSON pointer such as `/refresh_token`) and `name` (the secret) | optional |

Requests to private, loopback, and link-local addresses are always blocked.

```yaml
- name: notify
  type: http_request
  url: https://api.example.com/v1/reports
  method: POST
  secrets: [EXAMPLE_API_KEY]
  headers:
    Authorization: "Bearer {{ secrets.EXAMPLE_API_KEY }}"
    Content-Type: application/json
  body: '{"text": "Weekly report is ready"}'
  allow_hosts: [api.example.com]
```

## `type: airway`

Runs an Airway ELT pipeline (`.airway.yml`) as a step. The step completes only
once the pipeline's load has committed, so a following `execute_sql` task reads
fully loaded tables.

| Component | Description                                                         | Type     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| pipeline  | Path to the `.airway.yml` pipeline, relative to the project root     | required |
| resources | Subset of the pipeline's resources to run. Omit to run all of them  | optional |

```yaml
tasks:
  - name: ingest
    type: airway
    pipeline: pipelines/restaurant_analytics.airway.yml
    resources: [orders, order_checks]
  - name: sales_rollup
    type: execute_sql
    database: warehouse
    sql_file: rollups/sales_daily_metrics.sql
```

## Common task options

Any task can also take:

| Component | Description |
| --------- | ----------- |
| export    | Write the task's result to a file: `path` (relative to the project root; may use Jinja) and `format` (`csv` or `json` for tabular results; `sql` for `execute_sql` and `semantic_query`, which writes the executed SQL). |
| cache     | File-backed cache: `path` (may use Jinja) and `enabled` (default `true`). The first run writes the task's result to `path`; later runs skip the task and use the file's contents instead. Edit the file to change what downstream tasks see; delete it to regenerate. |

### Caching a task's output

`cache` is useful for LLM-generated artifacts you want to review and pin — for
example, SQL from an agent in [SQL output mode](#sql-output-mode). After the
first run, edits you make to the cached file are used on every later run.

<Note>
The `visualize` task type has been retired. Automations that still use it fail
with an "unknown task type" error — use an agent task instead.
</Note>
